newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide expands investment in urban areas.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide expands investment in urban areas.

text.p: Nationwide Insurance said Friday it will expand its investment in urban areas and change its underwriting guidelines to enhance its product offerings to owners of older and less expensive homes.

Nationwide, which has been in talks with the U.S. Justice Department over allegations of discrimination against minorities, said it will establish new sales and service offices in Baltimore, Cleveland and Philadelphia, in addition to those already operating in Chicago and San Antonio.
The company said it will make an initial $3 million investment in urban areas.
Jobs in those offices will be filled by neighborhood residents wherever possible, Nationwide said.
The three new cities, Baltimore, Cleveland and Philadephia, will each receive $1 million of that initial $3 million, Nationwide said.
Similar investments will be made in other cities as Nationwide expands its urban presence, the insurer said.
In addition, money for revitalization efforts will be made available to urban residents in the form of low-interest loans for home purchases and renovations, Nationwide said.
Community outreach programs will be established in the areas of consumer and safety education.
And the company said new and stronger relationships will be forged with community leaders and organizations to promote urban revitalization and development.
Nationwide said the underwriting changes announced Friday will be effective as of April 15 in Illinois, Texas, Maryland, Ohio and Pennsylvania, subject to regulatory approval.
Other states will follow, the company said.

"As we strive to strengthen our position as a leading insurance provider, the urban market represents an attractive source of business," said Richard Crabtree, president of Nationwide's property and casualty insurance companies.
"Serving this market effectively, while working to strengthen urban neighborhoods is a crucial part of Nationwide's business strategy," Crabtree said in a statement.
Nationwide also is committed to increasing its involvement as an active member of the communities it serves, said Lorraine Brock, associate vice president of Urban Markets Development for Nationwide.
"Nationwide is committed to addressing the needs of the African-American and Hispanic communities," Brock said in a statement.
"Through our Urban Initiative, we will help create stronger markets, effectively serve our potential customers and build true partnerships with urban America," she said.
Nationwide said its urban marketing initiative is an outgrowth of a broader plan, unveiled in 1994, which focuses on better serving customers and improving Nationwide's overall competitive position.

Nationwide said the first phase of the plan included a massive restructuring of the compnany's field operations from regional into state operations along with a consolidation of processing operations.
